pages.name: Using Skills
pages.html:
Using Skills for Dice Rolling Modifications: Skills are applied to rolls for actions where the character can use their expertise with the relevant Skill set to perform the action.

  • Characteristics and Skills: When rolling to use a Skill, the referee will dictate which Characteristic will determine the check along with the Skill, based on the circumstances of the Skill check.
  • Skill Rank: Apply the rank of the skill as a DM to a roll. A rank of 0 means +0DM to a roll, a rank of 1 is +1DM is applied, etc.
  • Untrained in a Skill: Performing a task that requires a Skill in which the character has no rank incurs a -3DM to reflect a lack of knowledge or familiarity with the subject matter.

Make Your Own Skills: The provided Skills are just basic examples of what some Skills could be in Spacer. However, the players and referees are encouraged to develop any other Skills they would like to have in place of any provided in this book or to make up new ones entirely to complement different sci-fi settings.

Using Skills as a Roleplaying Reference: The referee may allow Skill ranks to function as a benchmark for roleplaying situations where the characters need to utilize their expertise when interacting with NPCs or when a certain level of specialization is needed to understand a situation.

  • Example 1: A player can use their Rank 2 Computers to relate to another expert NPC to gain information about a computerized security system, just by having the expert NPC acknowledge that the character knows what they are talking about. A Rank 0 character may not understand how advanced computerized security systems function in order to have a meaningful dialog with an expert and thus the expert wouldn't bother engaging in such a topic with the character.
  • Example 2: In a gun duel, the player character has Ranged Combat (Short) 1 and is engaging with an NPC with a Ranged Combat (Short) 0. Roll to hit as normal. However, on the chance they both hit each other, the player character will hit first due to their Skill being a rank higher than the NPC, negating the NPC's hit, since they would succumb to their injury before firing.

Book p.28

pages.name: Skill Ranks
pages.html:
Skill RankKnowledge Level
UntrainedYou have minimal to zero experience or knowledge in this subject. Incur -3DM
Rank 0Basic: You only have received training and education on the Skill with minimal real world application of it.
Rank 1Practical: You have experience applying the Skill in practical ways outside of training.
Rank 2Proficient: You effectively demonstrate your practice and experience with the Skill.
Rank 3Professional Skill: You demonstrate an exceptional level of knowledge and performance of the subject matter.
Rank 4Advanced Skill: You have a deeper understanding of the Skill beyond its normal use, with the Skill being second nature.
Rank 5Mastery of the Skill: You have a deep level of expertise and authority regarding the subject matter.

Book p.28

pages.name: Skill Descriptions
pages.html:
• Basic Skills: Most Skills are basic Skills that apply the rank to any related roll as determined by the referee. These Skills are typically modified with a specific attribute dice modifier, as determined by the referee based on the character’s actions and descriptions of those actions.
  • Specialized Skills: Skills with sub-categories are considered specialized. This means when such a Skill is acquired at Rank 0, the player can apply that rank to any of the related specialty Skills. However, once the Skill is acquired again, the character must choose a specialized version of that Skill to excel in. For example; gaining a rank from 0 to 1 in Melee Combat allows the player to specialize in Blade at rank 1. However, If they don’t have Hand-to-Hand but must fight hand-to-hand, then they would use their melee combat skill at rank 0.

The following are descriptions of the Skills found in the provided character generation mini-game.

  • Admin: Used to navigate the bureaucracy of businesses, governments, and other cultural hierarchies.
  • Astrogation: Used to plot faster-than-light jump routes and related knowledge.
  • Athlete: This represents a character’s training in physical performance and conditioning.
  • Broker: Used to make business deals and negotiate work contracts.
  • Comms: Used for operating communication systems, sensors, or remotely operating vehicles or drones.
  • Computers: Used to navigate, program, repair, and hack computer systems, along with anything that is determined by computer systems, including robots.
  • Carouse: Used to meet people, connect with others, and gather information like gossip and rumors.
  • Crafting: Used to construct or fabricate objects from parts or scrap.
  • Deception: Used to lie, mislead, or otherwise manipulate a person.
  • Diplomacy: Used to negotiate deals or persuade characters for political and personal purposes.
  • Drive: Used to drive a terrestrial land vehicle. Once gaining a rank after Rank 0 in drive, choose to specialize in one of the following:
    • Civilian: Used for typical and common vehicles available to the general population, such as cars, motorcycles, etc.
    • Grav: Used for high-tech vehicles that float above the ground and have different handling properties from traction-based land vehicles.
    • Industrial: Used for industrial vehicles that require specific training for license.
    • Marine: Used for any water-based craft.
    • Military: Used for military-grade vehicles that the general civilian wouldn't have access to.
    • Misc: Used for dirt-drillers, walking mecha, or any other non-traditional vehicle forms, as determined by the referee.
  • Electronics: Used to understand, use, or repair electric devices or circuitry.
  • Engineering: Used for understanding, operating, and figuring out mechanical structural systems, or for maintaining and operating power systems.
  • Gambling: Used for interacting in games of chance with NPCs or any other situation where the character is playing the odds, as up to the referee.
  • Jack-of-All-Trades: Used to allow the character to attempt a single Skill they are not familiar with as rank 0 once per in-game week. Additional ranks of JoAT allows for additional attempts. Jack-of-all-Trades starts at rank 1.
  • Leadership: Allows a spacer to give commands to groups of NPCs, equal to 6 individuals per rank. All rolls are applied to morale, orders, and anything else where the character might have to take a leadership position. Successful rolls indicate the NPCs’ willingness to comply with said orders.
  • Legal: Used to interpret, understand, and navigate legal systems and related structures.
  • Mechanic: Used to repair machines work and modify them.
  • Medic: Used for performing first aid and administration of medical services
  • Melee Combat: You have received training in using weapons and/or your fists offensively. Once you gain a rank past zero, you must select one of the following specializations:
    • Blade: Used to wield swords, axes, and other bladed melee weapons.
    • Hand-to-Hand: Used for boxing, martial arts, grappling, and related actions.
    • Bludgeon: Used for bludgeoning weapons and polearms without blades.
  • Navigation: Used for charting and interpreting maps and directions.
  • Persuade: Used to negotiate with someone or a group of people to attempt to get them to become agreeable or accepting of an offer, on a personal level.
  • Pilot: Used for flying craft, both in an atmosphere and in a vacuum. Once gaining a rank after Rank 0 in Pilot, choose to specialize in one of the following:
    • Starship: Used for controlling any spacecraft in the vacuum of space, along with entry and exit of planetary atmospheres.
    • Aircraft: Used for piloting any non-starcraft vehicles capable of flight within an atmosphere.
  • Profession: When acquired, choose the professional focus of the PC to represent their ability to understand, navigate, or execute the responsibilities or tasks associated with that profession. For example, Scientist, where the Profession Skill is used to access and use laboratories, or Musician, using Profession to compose and perform music for an audience. This Skill is intentionally open-ended to allow players to have creative applications of this Skill, but cannot substitute for established Skills if other players have ranks in those. The referee has final say if a Profession rank allows the character to perform the profession in any given situation.
  • Ranged Combat: Used for wielding projectile weapons such as handguns, rifles, energy guns, crossbows, etc. Once Rank 0 has been achieved in this Skill, any additional Skill ranks are applied to one of the following:
    • Short: Used for handguns such as pistols and revolvers.
    • Stock: Used for guns that require two hands to use, such as rifles, carbines, or SMGs.
    • Energy: Used for high tech-level weapons that use energy instead of ballistics.
    • Archaic: Used for low tech-level weapons such as bows, crossbows, slings, throwing weapons, etc.
      • Example: If a character gets Rank 0 in basic training, then learns Ranged Combat (short), they know Ranged Combat 0 and Ranged Combat (Short) 1. If the character attempts to use any ranged weapon that isn’t short, they only apply the Rank 0 to the Skill roll.
  • Recon: Used to allow a character to be perceptive and scout ahead to find helpful information or to remain alert in potentially dangerous situations. Used to counteract surprise at the beginning of combat but can also be applied to searching an area for clues.
  • Stealth: Used to remain hidden while moving around. Used as a contest roll against any NPCs searching using Recon, but can also be used to set up take-downs or spying.
  • Steward: Used for service and hospitality-related activities for passengers along with maintaining the staterooms of a starship.
  • Streetwise: Used for the ability to to make connections and gather information through illicit connections and to have the knowledge of where to look for less-than-legal opportunities.
  • Tactics: Used in combat to gain a battlefield advantage. When using Tactics in combat, the spacer directing the tactics can apply the rank as a +1DM per rank to any other NPC or characters for the battle. General Tactics is acquired at Rank 0 but advancing Tactics requires the character to select a specialization:
    • Starship: Used for knowledge and execution of strategies using naval starships in space combat.
    • Vehicle: Typically used by army-trained individuals for the proper application of tactical advantages and disadvantages of vehicular combat in battle.
    • Squad: Used for small-unit combat tactics applied to on-foot operations. Common training for army and marines.
    • Zero-G: Used while engaged in zero-G melee or ranged combat. Rank 0 means no penalty to attacks in zero-G, while any additional ranks are applied to any combat action while in zero-G in place of Vaccsuit. This is a common skill set for marine officers to learn.
  • Vaccsuit: Used when wearing a vaccsuit, which can be restrictive. This Skill is also applied when moving around in zero-G since everyone using a vaccsuit learns to navigate with it on while moving in zero-G.

Book p.28-29
